abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to better discriminate metastasized (lymphogen/occult/both combined) from non-metastasized seminoma based on post-transcriptional changes examined in the peripheral blood. METHODS: Total RNAs including small RNAs were isolated from the peripheral blood of patients suffering from metastasized testicular tumours (lymphogen, n = 5, clinical stage IIb/c; occult, n = 5, clinical stage I) and non-metastasized patients (n = 5, clinical stage I). Small RNA next generation sequencing (SOLID, Life Technologies) was employed to examine post-transcriptional changes. We searched for small RNAs showing at least 50 reads and a significant ≥ 2-fold difference using peripheral blood small RNAs of non-metastasized tumours as the reference group. Candidate small RNAs were examined in univariate logistic regression analysis and combinations of two small RNAs were further examined using support vector machines. RESULTS: On average 1.3 x 10(7), 1.2 x 10(7) and 1.2 x 10(7) small RNA reads were detectable in non-metastasized, lymphogen and occult metastasized seminoma, respectively of which 73-76% remained after trimming. From these between 80-82% represented annotated reads and 7.2-7.8% (1.6-1.7 x 10(4)) were annotated small RNA tags. Of them 137 small RNAs showed > 50 reads and a ≥ two-fold difference to the reference. In univariate analysis we detected 33-35 different small RNAs which significantly discriminated lymphogen/occult/combined metastasized from non-metastasized seminoma and among these different comparisons it were the same small RNAs in 44-79%. Many combinations of two of these small RNAs completely discriminated metastasized from non-metastasized seminoma irrespective of the metastasis subtype. CONCLUSIONS: Metastasized (either lymphogen or occult) seminoma can be completely discriminated from non-metastasized seminoma with a combination of two small RNAs measured in the peripheral blood.
abstract_ja: 背景：末梢血における転写後変化を基に、転移性(リンパ節性・潜在性・両者を合わせたもの)と非転移性セミノーマをより良く識別することを目的とした。方法：転移性精巣腫瘍患者(リンパ節性 n=5、臨床病期IIb/c；潜在性 n=5、臨床病期I)および非転移性患者(n=5、臨床病期I)の末梢血から、小分子RNAを含む総RNAを単離した。転写後変化の検討には小分子RNAの次世代シーケンス(SOLID、Life Technologies)を用いた。非転移性腫瘍の末梢血小分子RNAを基準群として、少なくとも50リードかつ有意な2倍以上の差を示す小分子RNAを探索した。候補小分子RNAは単変量ロジスティック回帰分析で検討し、そのうち2種類の組み合わせはサポートベクターマシンで検討した。結果：非転移性、リンパ節性転移、潜在性転移のセミノーマで、平均してそれぞれ約1.3×10^7、1.2×10^7、1.2×10^7の小分子RNAリードが検出され、トリミング後に73-76%が残った。このうち80-82%がアノテーション付きリードであり、7.2-7.8%(1.6-1.7×10^4)がアノテーション付き小分子RNAタグであった。このうち137種の小分子RNAが、基準に対して50リード以上かつ2倍以上の差を示した。単変量解析では、リンパ節性・潜在性・両者を合わせた転移性セミノーマを非転移性セミノーマから有意に識別する小分子RNAを33-35種検出し、各比較間で同一の小分子RNAが44-79%を占めた。これら小分子RNAのうち2種類を組み合わせた多くの組み合わせが、転移のサブタイプにかかわらず、転移性セミノーマと非転移性セミノーマを完全に識別した。結論：リンパ節性または潜在性の転移性セミノーマは、末梢血で測定した2種類の小分子RNAの組み合わせにより、非転移性セミノーマと完全に識別できる。
